candidate.title: CIP-TAP
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina CIP-TAP schematic for identifying capped small RNA (csRNA) species: mixed small-RNA end classes undergo CIP, 3′ linker ligation/gel purification, TAP, 5′ linker ligation/gel purification, cDNA synthesis, PCR and final purification. Rows denote chemical classes in the same sample, not separately processed libraries. The Gu et al. full text supports the small-RNA CIP-TAP implementation and clarifies the selection chemistry. CapSeq, CIP-PNK, TAP-only cloning and catalogue-listed kits are not additional targets of this schematic. The paper’s upstream input sizing clarifies the material boundary without adding an unshown operation; sequencing is the downstream readout, beyond the last drawn cDNA state.

states.label: Small-RNA input containing capped and uncapped end classes
features: Purple RNA bodies are shown with 5′P, 5′OH, 5′PPP and 5′GPPP end labels. The GPPP symbol denotes the capped target class; it does not specify cap methylation.
The left caption is CIP-TAP for identifying capped small RNA (csRNA) species. Yellow highlighting identifies the capped target in an explanatory icon, not a depicted purification step.
The paper-supported implementation starts with size-fractionated 18–40 nt RNA from total RNA. This clarifies the small-RNA input boundary; upstream size selection is not drawn as an operation.

states.label: Purified cDNA library, final depicted product
features: Black line at the far right is labelled cDNA and follows Purification.

The readout carrier for downstream sequencing is DNA derived from small RNA. Sequence reads can identify recovered small-RNA sequences and map their 5′ ends at nucleotide resolution, supporting candidate start-site/csRNA interpretation.

Enrichment is imperfect: the paper reports residual mature miRNA/piRNA reads and no significant change in relative 22G-RNA recovery versus CIP-PNK. Recovery alone does not establish that every insert was capped, Pol II-derived or a piRNA precursor.
PCR amplification can bias representation and introduce polymerase errors, as noted by the catalogue. No UMI-based molecular counting or barcode-defined biological association is shown.

operations.label: CIP
operations.description: Treat the input RNA mixture with calf intestinal phosphatase. The uncapped 5′P and 5′PPP classes become 5′OH, while the capped class remains capped and the existing 5′OH class remains 5′OH.
operations.mechanism: CIP removes exposed 5′ mono- or triphosphates. CIP is a catalyst/treatment reagent, not a retained library molecule.
operations.information_effect: Reduces subsequent 5′ linker accessibility of uncapped RNA while preserving the cap-protected class; the RNA sequence remains the carrier of target identity.

operations.label: 3′ primer ligation / Gel purify
operations.description: Attach the 3′ linker to both displayed RNA classes and gel-purify the ligation products. This changes the RNA 3′ interface without changing the depicted 5′OH-versus-capped distinction.
operations.mechanism: 3′-end linker ligation followed by gel purification, kept as the single captioned block. The schematic does not specify internal ligation chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a common downstream linker interface on the RNA molecules; this step does not itself select caps.

Results, b00024

operations.label: TAP
operations.description: Treat the already 3′-linked RNA with tobacco acid pyrophosphatase. The capped class is decapped to 5′ monophosphate; the displayed uncapped 5′OH class stays 5′OH.
operations.mechanism: TAP removes the 5′ cap, exposing a 5′ monophosphate for 5′ linker ligation. TAP is a catalyst/treatment reagent, not the sequenced product.
operations.information_effect: Converts prior cap protection into differential 5′ linker competence. The cap itself is lost, while the original RNA sequence and 5′ boundary are retained in the intended library route.

operations.label: 5′ primer ligation / gel purify
operations.description: Attach the orange 5′ linker to the TAP-generated 5′P RNA and gel-purify. The drawing also retains an upper 5′OH/3′-linked class without the orange linker. The two output state records distinguish co-resident chemical populations, not a physical split or separate processing.
operations.mechanism: 5′ linker ligation uses the monophosphate exposed by decapping. The 5′OH class is disfavored for this interface. Linker sequence and activation chemistry are not specified in the schematic.
operations.information_effect: Flanks the productive capped-origin RNA insert with two linker interfaces. Their ordered attachment preserves the sequence boundary of the original RNA; residual non-target recovery remains possible.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven captioned transformation blocks belong to the sole named target, CIP-TAP. The two RNA rows after CIP are co-resident end classes of one workflow, supported by the paper’s treatment of the sample; they are not alternatives requiring separate operation instances. The paper describes a separate CIP-PNK control and a CapSeq workflow, neither of which is depicted here. Its native 18–40 nt small-RNA CIP-TAP route matches the drawn sequence. This establishes the scoped implementation, not identity of every protocol called CIP-TAP.
